findings.short_summary: "Run health check" always fails (code E-400)
findings.summary: The Diagnostics screen's "Run health check" action deterministically reports failure with 'Health check failed (code E-400)' on every invocation.
findings.failure_scenario: Navigate Home > About > Diagnostics > tap 'Run health check'. Result is always 'Health check failed (code E-400)', 100% reproducible across repeated taps and app restarts. A diagnostic self-test that always fails is either a real regression in the health-check logic or a broken/stubbed check that should not ship visibly failing — either way it will alarm anyone who runs it and erodes trust in the diagnostics screen.

findings.short_summary: Redeem accepts an empty/blank promo code as valid
findings.summary: Tapping 'Redeem' with an empty Promo code field still reports 'Promo applied', i.e. there is no input validation on the promo code field.
findings.failure_scenario: On Checkout, clear the Promo code field entirely (or leave it untouched) and tap 'Redeem'. The app reports 'Promo applied' with no error, identical to submitting a real-looking code, so users (and any downstream logic keyed off that message) cannot distinguish a real redemption from a no-op.

findings.short_summary: Discounted total does not match base price × quantity under any simple rule
findings.summary: After 'Apply discount', the displayed Total does not correspond to a consistent discount formula relative to Base price ($9.37/unit) × Quantity: qty 1→$9, 2→$17, 3→$25, 4→$32, implying an effective 'discount' percentage that grows irregularly with quantity rather than following a fixed rate or fixed amount.
findings.failure_scenario: Set Quantity to 1/2/3/4 and tap Apply discount each time (fresh launch to avoid any stacking). The resulting totals (9, 17, 25, 32) don't match floor(9.37*qty) minus any constant % or constant amount, so the pricing math looks implemented incorrectly rather than as an intentional bulk-discount curve; a paying user would see an unexplainable and unverifiable total since no pre-discount subtotal is ever shown.

findings.short_summary: "Export" button gives no feedback
findings.summary: Tapping 'Export' on an item detail screen produces no visible result — no toast, dialog, share sheet, or state change.
findings.failure_scenario: Catalog > Item 001 > tap Export. Screen is pixel-identical before and after; a user has no way to know whether the export succeeded, failed, or does nothing at all.

findings.short_summary: Form submit (play) button gives no feedback
findings.summary: The unlabeled submit/play button on the Form screen produces no visible confirmation, error, or navigation after tapping, even with valid input filled in (Name, Subscribe, Tier).
findings.failure_scenario: Fill Name='Test User', toggle Subscribe on, set Tier='Max', tap the play-icon button at the bottom. No toast/snackbar/navigation appears, so the user cannot tell if the form was submitted.

findings.short_summary: "Retry sync" gives no feedback
findings.summary: Tapping 'Retry sync' under Sync status produces no visible change to the 'Sync idle' label or any other on-screen feedback.
findings.failure_scenario: About > Diagnostics > tap 'Retry sync'. The status text remains 'Sync idle' with no transient 'syncing' state or completion message, making it indistinguishable from a dead button.

findings.summary: Tapping 'Redeem' with an empty Promo code field still reports 'Promo applied', i.e. there is no input validation on the promo code field.
findings.failure_scenario: On Checkout, clear the Promo code field entirely (or leave it untouched) and tap 'Redeem'. findings.short_summary: Discounted total does not match base price × quantity under any simple rule
findings.summary: After 'Apply discount', the displayed Total does not correspond to a consistent discount formula relative to Base price ($9.37/unit) × Quantity: qty 1→$9, 2→$17, 3→$25, 4→$32, implying an effective 'discount' percentage that grows irregularly with quantity rather than following a fixed rate or fixed amount.
findings.failure_scenario: Set Quantity to 1/2/3/4 and tap Apply discount each time (fresh launch to avoid any stacking). The resulting totals (9, 17, 25, 32) don't match floor(9.37*qty) minus any constant % or constant amount, so the pricing math looks implemented incorrectly rather than as an intentional bulk-discount curve; a paying user would see an unexplainable and unverifiable total since no pre-discount subtotal is ever shown.

## Verdict: **DO NOT SHIP**

I exercised all five sections of the app (Catalog, Form, About/Diagnostics, Checkout, Orders) on the real device. Most of the app works correctly — the Catalog list (100 items, scrolls and terminates cleanly), the Form's dropdown/toggle/text input, and the Orders archive flow (long-press → confirmation dialog → correct removal) all behave exactly as expected, and the app survives backgrounding/relaunch without crashing.

However, I found a blocking defect and several lesser ones:

1. **"Run health check" on the Diagnostics screen always fails** with "Health check failed (code E-400)" — 100% reproducible on every tap and after app restart. A self-test that deterministically fails is the kind of thing that should not reach a release candidate; it will read as a broken build to anyone who opens Diagnostics.
2. **Checkout's discount math looks wrong**: applying the discount at quantities 1–4 against the stated $9.37/unit base price yields totals ($9, $17, $25, $32) that don't follow any consistent percentage or flat-amount discount rule, and no pre-discount subtotal is ever shown to let a user sanity-check it.
3. **"Redeem" accepts a blank promo code** and reports "Promo applied" with zero validation.
4. Three buttons give **no feedback at all** when tapped: Catalog item "Export", the Form screen's submit (play) button, and Diagnostics' "Retry sync" — all look like dead buttons from the UI alone.

The health-check failure alone is release-blocking for a diagnostics feature; combined with the pricing inconsistency and silent buttons, this build needs another pass before shipping.
